  regulatory_minimum_cet1_ratio decimal(8,4) [note: 'Regulatory minimum CET1 ratio requirement applicable to the institution, expressed as a percentage.']
  reporting_entity_name varchar [note: 'Legal name of the bank holding company or financial institution submitting the capital plan.']
  scenario_type varchar [note: 'Type of stress scenario applied in this capital plan (base, adverse, severely adverse, or custom internal scenario).']
  stress_loss_projection_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'Total projected losses under the stress scenario over the planning horizon, in millions of base currency.']
  submission_date date [note: 'Date the capital plan was submitted to the Federal Reserve for CCAR/DFAST review.']

  Note: 'Multi-year capital planning record capturing projected CET1 ratios, RWA growth assumptions, dividend and buyback plans, stress scenario capital trajectories, and capital actions (issuance, redemption, AT1 triggers) under base and adverse scenarios. Submitted to the Federal Reserve as part of CCAR/DFAST annual capital planning cycle. Tracks ALCO-approved capital targets and management buffers above regulatory minimums.'
}

Table treasury.funding_plan {
  funding_plan_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique identifier for the funding plan record. Primary key for the funding plan entity.']
  accounting_period_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to ledger.accounting_period. Business justification: Funding plans executed within specific accounting periods for budget tracking, variance analysis, and cost of funds reporting. Links funding strategy to fiscal period performance measurement.']
  alco_meeting_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to treasury.alco_meeting. Business justification: Funding plans (wholesale and retail funding strategy, debt issuance plans) are strategic treasury decisions made by ALCO. The funding_plan product has approval_date and approved_by attributes but lack']
  currency_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to reference.currency. Business justification: Funding plans specify issuance currency for debt issuance strategy. Link enables multi-currency funding diversification, FX hedging decisions, and currency-specific cost of funds analysis.']
  actual_cost_of_funds_rate decimal(10,6) [note: 'Actual realized all-in cost of funds rate for this instrument type during the plan period, expressed as a decimal. Tracks execution vs. target pricing.']
  actual_issuance_amount decimal(20,2) [note: 'Actual notional amount raised through this funding instrument during the plan period, in the plan\'s base currency. Tracks execution vs. plan.']
  approved_by varchar [note: 'Name or identifier of the ALCO member or executive who approved the funding plan.']
  business_unit varchar [note: 'Business unit or line of business (LOB) responsible for managing this funding plan or debt issuance (e.g., Corporate Treasury, Capital Markets, Retail Banking).']
  call_date date [note: 'Earliest date on which the issuer can exercise the call option to redeem the debt instrument. Null if not callable.']
  call_feature_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the debt instrument includes a call feature allowing the issuer to redeem the instrument before maturity. True if callable, False otherwise.']
  comments varchar [note: 'Free-text field for additional notes, commentary, or context regarding the funding plan or specific issuance (e.g., market conditions, strategic rationale, execution challenges).']
  concentration_limit_percentage decimal(5,2) [note: 'Maximum allowable percentage of total funding that can be sourced from this instrument type, as defined by ALCO policy. Used to enforce diversification and concentration risk limits.']
  counterparty_concentration_limit decimal(20,2) [note: 'Maximum notional amount that can be sourced from a single counterparty or investor group for this instrument type, in the plan\'s base currency. Enforces counterparty concentration risk limits.']
  coupon_rate decimal(10,6) [note: 'Annual coupon rate for the debt instrument, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.0425 for 4.25%). For floating-rate instruments, this represents the spread over the reference rate.']
  coupon_type varchar [note: 'Type of coupon structure for the debt instrument: fixed (constant rate), floating (variable rate linked to benchmark), zero-coupon (no periodic interest), step-up (increasing rate schedule), callable (issuer redemption option), or puttable (investor redemption option).']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this funding plan record was first created in the system. ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX).']
  cusip varchar [note: 'Committee on Uniform Securities Identification Procedures (CUSIP) identifier for the specific debt issuance, if applicable. 9-character alphanumeric code used in North America.']
  instrument_type varchar [note: 'Type of funding instrument covered by this plan entry (e.g., senior unsecured bonds, covered bonds, Federal Home Loan Bank (FHLB) advances, repurchase agreements (repo), retail deposits, commercial paper (CP), certificates of deposit (CDs), subordinated debt). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: senior_unsecured|covered_bonds|fhlb_advances|repo|deposits|commercial_paper|certificates_of_deposit|subordinated_debt|tier2_capital|preferred_stock — promote to reference product]']
  isin varchar [note: 'International Securities Identification Number (ISIN) for the specific debt issuance, if applicable. 12-character alphanumeric code (ISO 6166 standard).']
  issuance_date date [note: 'Actual date on which the debt instrument was issued to investors. Represents the trade date for the issuance.']
  last_modified_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this funding plan record was last updated in the system. ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX).']
  lcr_treatment varchar [note: 'Classification of the funding source for Liquidity Coverage Ratio (LCR) calculation purposes: stable (retail deposits with low run-off), less-stable (higher run-off), operational (operational deposits), non-operational (wholesale funding), or excluded (not included in LCR).']
  legal_entity_identifier varchar [note: '20-character Legal Entity Identifier (LEI) of the issuing legal entity. ISO 17442 standard identifier for regulatory reporting.']
  listing_exchange varchar [note: 'Name of the stock exchange or trading venue where the debt instrument is listed (e.g., New York Stock Exchange (NYSE), London Stock Exchange (LSE), Luxembourg Stock Exchange). Null if unlisted.']
  maturity_date date [note: 'Scheduled maturity date of the debt instrument, when principal repayment is due. May be subject to call/put features.']
  notional_outstanding decimal(20,2) [note: 'Current outstanding notional principal amount of the debt instrument, in the instrument\'s currency. Tracks amortization and prepayments.']
  nsfr_treatment varchar [note: 'Classification of the funding source for Net Stable Funding Ratio (NSFR) calculation purposes: stable (high available stable funding factor), less-stable (lower factor), wholesale (institutional funding), or excluded (not included in NSFR).']
  plan_name varchar [note: 'Business name or title of the funding plan (e.g., \'FY2024 Q2 Wholesale Funding Strategy\', \'2024 Annual Debt Issuance Plan\').']
  plan_period_end_date date [note: 'The effective end date of the funding plan period (e.g., end of fiscal quarter or year).']
  plan_period_start_date date [note: 'The effective start date of the funding plan period (e.g., beginning of fiscal quarter or year).']
  plan_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the funding plan: draft (under development), approved (ALCO-approved), active (in execution), executed (fully completed), closed (archived), or cancelled (terminated before execution).']
  plan_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the funding plan by strategic purpose: wholesale (institutional funding), retail (deposit-based), hybrid (mixed sources), contingency (stress scenario), or strategic (long-term capital structure).']
  put_date date [note: 'Earliest date on which the investor can exercise the put option to demand redemption. Null if not puttable.']
  put_feature_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the debt instrument includes a put feature allowing the investor to demand early redemption. True if puttable, False otherwise.']
  reference_rate decimal(18,2) [note: 'Benchmark reference rate for floating-rate instruments (e.g., Secured Overnight Financing Rate (SOFR), London Interbank Offered Rate (LIBOR), Euro Interbank Offered Rate (EURIBOR)). Null for fixed-rate instruments.']
  regulatory_capital_treatment varchar [note: 'Classification of the funding instrument for regulatory capital purposes: Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1), Additional Tier 1 (Tier1), Tier 2 (Tier2), non-capital (does not qualify), or excluded (not applicable).']
  target_cost_of_funds_rate decimal(10,6) [note: 'Planned or target all-in cost of funds rate for this instrument type, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.0325 for 3.25% or 325 basis points). Includes coupon, fees, and issuance costs.']
  target_issuance_amount decimal(20,2) [note: 'Planned or target notional amount to be raised through this funding instrument during the plan period, in the plan\'s base currency.']
  target_maturity_profile varchar [note: 'Planned maturity profile for the funding instrument: short-term (< 1 year), medium-term (1-5 years), long-term (> 5 years), perpetual (no maturity), or mixed (diversified maturities).']
  target_weighted_average_maturity_years decimal(10,2) [note: 'Planned weighted average maturity of the funding instrument issuances, expressed in years. Used for maturity ladder and duration management.']
  underwriter_name varchar [note: 'Name of the lead underwriter or bookrunner for the debt issuance (e.g., investment bank managing the offering).']
  variance_amount decimal(20,2) [note: 'Difference between actual and target issuance amounts (actual minus target). Positive indicates over-execution; negative indicates under-execution.']

  Note: 'Treasury funding strategy, execution, and debt issuance record capturing the banks wholesale and retail funding plan by instrument type (senior unsecured, covered bonds, FHLB advances, repo, deposits, commercial paper, CDs), target issuance volumes, maturity profile, currency mix, and cost-of-funds targets. Includes individual debt issuance execution records: ISIN/CUSIP, issuance date, maturity, coupon type/rate, currency, notional outstanding, underwriter, listing exchange, call/put features, and outstanding balance tracking. Tracks actual vs. planned funding execution, concentration limits by counterparty and instrument, and feeds into the funding maturity profile and capital structure reporting. Approved by ALCO and updated quarterly. Post-merge: this is the single source of truth for funding strategy and debt issuance — replaces former separate debt_issuance product.'
}

  legal_entity_identifier varchar [note: '20-character ISO 17442 Legal Entity Identifier of the issuing bank entity. Used for regulatory reporting and counterparty identification.']

  legal_entity_code varchar [note: 'Code identifying the legal entity or consolidation level to which this transfer pricing curve applies. Supports multi-entity treasury operations.']
  liquidity_spread_bps decimal(10,2) [note: 'The bank-specific liquidity premium adjustment in basis points added to the benchmark rate to reflect the institution\'s funding liquidity costs and liquidity risk.']
  market_data_source varchar [note: 'The external market data provider or system from which benchmark rates were sourced (e.g., Bloomberg, Refinitiv, Federal Reserve, internal trading desk).']
  market_data_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The timestamp at which the underlying market benchmark rates were observed or extracted for curve construction.']
  nsfr_treatment_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this curve is used in Net Stable Funding Ratio (NSFR) calculations and reporting. True if applicable, false otherwise.']
  operational_spread_bps decimal(10,2) [note: 'Additional spread in basis points to cover operational costs, capital allocation, and other bank-specific adjustments not captured in liquidity or credit spreads.']
  rate_basis_points decimal(10,2) [note: 'The transfer pricing rate expressed in basis points (e.g., 525 BPS for 5.25%). One basis point equals 0.01%. Provided for convenience and reporting clarity.']
  rate_value decimal(12,8) [note: 'The transfer pricing rate expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.0525 for 5.25%). This is the internal rate used for funds transfer pricing calculations at this tenor point.']
  regulatory_treatment varchar [note: 'Description of how this transfer pricing curve aligns with or supports regulatory capital, liquidity, or risk management requirements (e.g., LCR, NSFR, IRRBB, CECL).']
  source_system varchar [note: 'The name or identifier of the upstream treasury management system or curve construction platform that generated or published this transfer pricing curve.']
  stress_scenario_type varchar [note: 'If this curve represents a stress or scenario-based variant, this field identifies the stress scenario (e.g., baseline, adverse, severely adverse, CCAR, DFAST, custom stress). Null for base case curves.']
  tenor_bucket varchar [note: 'The maturity tenor point on the yield curve for which the rate is defined (e.g., overnight, 1 month, 3 months, 1 year, 5 years). Represents the term structure dimension of the curve. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: overnight|1W|1M|3M|6M|9M|1Y|2Y|3Y|5Y|7Y|10Y|15Y|20Y|30Y — 15 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  usage_scope varchar [note: 'Description of the intended use cases and applications for this transfer pricing curve (e.g., loan pricing, deposit pricing, balance sheet optimization, profitability analysis, capital allocation).']

  Note: 'Internal FTP yield curve master capturing the term structure of internal transfer rates by currency, tenor, and curve type (base rate curve, liquidity spread curve, credit spread curve). Built from market benchmarks (SOFR, OIS, swap rates) and adjusted for bank-specific liquidity premiums. Versioned by effective date and ALCO approval cycle. Used as the foundational input for all FTP rate calculations across the bank.'
}

  nsfr_impact_percentage decimal(10,6) [note: 'Estimated percentage point impact on the Net Stable Funding Ratio (NSFR) under this stress scenario, expressed as a decimal (e.g., -0.15 for 15 percentage point decline).']
  regulatory_classification varchar [note: 'Regulatory framework classification: CCAR severely adverse, CCAR adverse, DFAST adverse, internal (proprietary), or other.']
  regulatory_submission_flag boolean [note: 'Boolean flag indicating whether this stress scenario is used for regulatory submissions (CCAR, DFAST, or other supervisory stress testing). True if submitted to regulators, False otherwise.']
  response_action_summary varchar [note: 'High-level summary of pre-approved liquidity stress response actions defined in the contingency funding plan for this scenario (e.g., \'Activate FHLB advances, reduce new lending, sell liquid securities portfolio\').']
  retail_deposit_runoff_rate decimal(10,6) [note: 'Assumed percentage rate of retail deposit outflows under this stress scenario, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.15 for 15% runoff).']
  scenario_code varchar [note: 'Short alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the scenario for reporting and system integration.']
  scenario_description varchar [note: 'Detailed narrative description of the stress scenario, including macroeconomic assumptions, market conditions, and firm-specific stress drivers.']
  scenario_name varchar [note: 'Business name of the stress scenario (e.g., \'Q1 2024 CCAR Severely Adverse\', \'Idiosyncratic Deposit Run\', \'Market-Wide Credit Crisis\').']
  scenario_severity_rating varchar [note: 'Qualitative severity rating of the stress scenario: mild, moderate, severe, or extreme, based on the magnitude of assumed shocks and impacts.']
  scenario_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the stress scenario: draft (under development), active (approved for use), archived (historical), superseded (replaced by newer version).']
  scenario_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the stress scenario: idiosyncratic (firm-specific), market-wide (systemic), combined (both), or custom (internal ad-hoc).']
  secured_funding_haircut_rate decimal(10,6) [note: 'Additional haircut percentage applied to collateral values for secured funding transactions under stress, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.25 for 25% additional haircut).']
  stress_horizon_days varchar [note: 'Duration of the stress scenario in days (e.g., 30, 90, 365) over which liquidity and capital impacts are projected.']
  version_number varchar [note: 'Version number of this stress scenario, incremented with each material update or revision. Supports scenario version control and audit trail.']
  wholesale_deposit_runoff_rate decimal(10,6) [note: 'Assumed percentage rate of wholesale deposit outflows under this stress scenario, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.40 for 40% runoff).']
  wholesale_funding_rollover_rate decimal(10,6) [note: 'Assumed percentage of maturing wholesale funding that can be successfully rolled over under stress, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.50 for 50% rollover success).']

  Note: 'Liquidity and capital stress scenario definitions and contingency funding response plans. Scenario attributes: scenario name (idiosyncratic, market-wide, combined), stress horizon, assumed deposit runoff rates, wholesale funding rollover assumptions, asset haircuts, drawdown rates on committed facilities, and regulatory classification (CCAR severely adverse, DFAST adverse, internal). Contingency Funding Plan (CFP) attributes: pre-approved liquidity stress response actions, early warning indicators (EWIs), trigger thresholds, escalation procedures, and available contingent liquidity sources (central bank facilities, FHLB, asset monetization). Reviewed and approved by ALCO annually. Required by Federal Reserve SR 10-6 and OCC guidance on liquidity risk management. Used as input parameters for LCR stress testing, cash flow forecasting, and CCAR/DFAST capital projections.'
}

Primary transactional entity of the ledger domain supporting the full GL posting lifecycle including automated posting rules, approval workflows, and audit trail for SOX Section 302/404 compliance.'

  variance_root_cause varchar [note: 'Documented root cause explanation for any variance between subledger and General Ledger (GL) balances (e.g., timing difference, posting error, unrecorded transaction).']

  Note: 'Registry of subledger modules that feed into the general ledger, combined with the operational reconciliation records that verify subledger-to-GL integrity each period. Captures subledger configuration: name, type (accounts payable, accounts receivable, fixed assets, loans, securities, payroll, derivatives), source system, GL transfer method, posting frequency, and control account mapping. Also captures period-end reconciliation execution: reconciliation run ID, accounting period, GL account range, subledger aggregate balance, GL posted balance, variance amount, variance root cause, reconciliation status (reconciled, in-progress, exception, escalated), auto-reconciliation flag, preparer, reviewer, approval date, resolution actions, and SOX control evidence reference. This product is the single source of truth for both subledger configuration and subledger-to-GL reconciliation governance, supporting period-end close compliance for SOX Section 302/404 and external audit requirements.'
}

  tax_loss_carryforward_amount decimal(20,2) [note: 'Cumulative tax loss carryforwards available to offset future taxable income.']
  temporary_difference_amount decimal(20,2) [note: 'Total temporary differences between book basis and tax basis of assets and liabilities that will reverse in future periods.']
  total_tax_expense_amount decimal(20,2) [note: 'Total income tax expense for the period, sum of current and deferred tax expense.']
  unrecognized_tax_benefit_amount decimal(20,2) [note: 'Amount of tax benefit from uncertain tax positions that does not meet the recognition threshold under FIN 48 / IFRIC 23.']
  valuation_allowance_amount decimal(20,2) [note: 'Valuation allowance established to reduce deferred tax assets to the amount that is more likely than not to be realized.']

  Note: 'Tax provision and deferred tax calculation record. Captures current tax expense, deferred tax assets/liabilities, effective tax rate, and reconciliation to statutory rate.'
}

Table ledger.account_testing_scope {
  account_testing_scope_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique identifier for this account testing scope record']
  engagement_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the internal audit engagement under which this account is being tested']
  gl_account_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the general ledger account selected for testing in this engagement']
  account_testing_status varchar [note: 'Current status of testing for this GL account within this engagement lifecycle']
  auditor_notes varchar [note: 'Free-text notes documenting observations, issues, or context specific to testing this GL account during this engagement']
  findings_count varchar [note: 'Number of audit findings or exceptions identified during testing of this GL account in this engagement']
  materiality_threshold decimal(18,2) [note: 'Monetary threshold used to determine the significance of misstatements or control deficiencies identified in this GL account during this engagement']
  risk_rating varchar [note: 'Risk rating assigned to this specific GL account within the context of this engagement, reflecting inherent risk, control risk, and detection risk']
  sample_size varchar [note: 'Number of transactions or journal entries selected for detailed testing from this GL account during this engagement']
  sampling_methodology varchar [note: 'The audit sampling approach applied to this GL account for this engagement, such as statistical sampling, judgmental sampling, or monetary unit sampling']
  scope_rationale varchar [note: 'Business justification for including this GL account in the engagement scope, such as materiality, risk profile, regulatory requirement, or prior audit findings']
  testing_completion_date date [note: 'Date when audit testing procedures for this GL account were completed for this engagement']
  testing_period_end_date date [note: 'End date of the period for which transactions in this GL account will be tested during this engagement']
  testing_period_start_date date [note: 'Start date of the period for which transactions in this GL account will be tested during this engagement']
  testing_procedures varchar [note: 'Specific audit procedures to be performed on this GL account during this engagement, such as substantive testing, control testing, reconciliation review, or analytical procedures']

  Note: 'This association product represents the audit scope relationship between gl_account and engagement. It captures the specific GL accounts selected for testing within each internal audit engagement, including the rationale for inclusion, risk assessment, sampling methodology, testing period, and materiality thresholds. Each record links one GL account to one engagement with attributes that exist only in the context of this specific audit scope decision.. Existence Justification: In banking internal audit operations, each audit engagement tests multiple GL accounts based on risk assessment, materiality, and regulatory requirements, and each GL account may be tested across multiple engagements over time (annual audits, SOX testing, regulatory exams, targeted reviews). The audit team actively manages the scope selection for each engagement, documenting why specific accounts are included, the risk rating for each account in that engagement context, the sampling approach, testing period, and materiality thresholds. This is a recognized business process called \'audit scope definition\' or \'account testing scope.\''
}

  disposition varchar [note: 'Final determination of the alert outcome after analyst review: true positive (suspicious activity confirmed), false positive (benign activity), escalated to case for further investigation, or pending review.']
  escalation_reason varchar [note: 'Explanation provided by the analyst for escalating the alert to a full case investigation, detailing the suspicious indicators and risk factors identified.']
  high_risk_geography_flag boolean [note: 'Indicator whether the alert involves transactions with countries or jurisdictions identified as high-risk for money laundering or terrorist financing per FATF or internal risk ratings.']
  lookback_period_days varchar [note: 'Number of days in the historical window analyzed by the detection scenario to identify the suspicious pattern.']
  model_version varchar [note: 'Version identifier of the machine learning model or rule set used by the detection engine at the time the alert was generated, supporting model governance and audit trails.']
  pep_flag boolean [note: 'Indicator whether the customer or beneficial owner associated with the alert is classified as a Politically Exposed Person, requiring enhanced due diligence.']
  priority varchar [note: 'Priority level assigned to the alert based on risk score, customer risk rating, and scenario severity, guiding the order of analyst review.']
  review_completion_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when the analyst completed the review and assigned a disposition to the alert.']
  review_start_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when the analyst began reviewing the alert, marking the start of the investigation workflow.']
  risk_score decimal(5,2) [note: 'Quantitative risk score assigned by the detection engine indicating the severity or likelihood of money laundering activity, typically on a 0-100 or 0-1000 scale.']
  sar_filed_flag boolean [note: 'Indicator whether a Suspicious Activity Report was filed with FinCEN as a result of this alert and subsequent investigation.']
  sar_filing_date date [note: 'Date when the Suspicious Activity Report was filed with FinCEN, if applicable.']
  sla_deadline timestamp [note: 'Target date and time by which the alert must be reviewed and dispositioned per internal SLA policies and regulatory requirements.']
  source_system varchar [note: 'Name of the AML transaction monitoring platform that generated the alert (e.g., NICE Actimize, Oracle Financial Crime, SAS AML).']
  total_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'Aggregate monetary value of all transactions associated with the alert, expressed in the account\'s base currency.']
  transaction_count varchar [note: 'Number of transactions that contributed to the alert generation, indicating the volume of suspicious activity detected.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when the alert record was last modified, capturing changes to status, disposition, or analyst assignments.']

  Note: 'AML transaction monitoring alert generated by the financial crime detection engine (NICE Actimize, Oracle Financial Crime, or equivalent) when a customer transaction pattern, behavior anomaly, or network relationship triggers a detection rule, scenario, or machine learning model threshold. Captures alert type (structuring, rapid movement, high-risk geography, unusual activity), risk score, triggering rule/scenario ID, entity under review (customer, account, counterparty), alert status (new, assigned, under-review, escalated, closed), disposition (true positive, false positive, escalated to case), assigned analyst, assignment date, and SLA deadline. Primary operational record driving the Level 1 alert review workflow in AML transaction monitoring.'
}

  auditor_notes varchar [note: 'Free-text observations, findings, and contextual notes recorded by the auditor during validation testing of this rule.']
  exceptions_identified varchar [note: 'Number of control exceptions or deficiencies identified during testing of this monitoring rule in this engagement.']
  false_positive_rate_observed decimal(5,4) [note: 'Percentage of alerts generated by this rule during the audit period that were determined to be false positives, as measured during engagement testing. Explicitly identified in detection reasoning.']
  last_validation_date date [note: 'Date when this specific rule validation testing was completed during the engagement. Explicitly identified in detection reasoning.']
  rule_effectiveness_rating varchar [note: 'Audit assessment of the monitoring rule\'s effectiveness in detecting the intended risk scenarios during the engagement testing period. Explicitly identified in detection reasoning.']
  sample_size varchar [note: 'Number of transactions or alerts sampled for testing this rule during the engagement, supporting the statistical validity of validation results.']
  tuning_recommendations varchar [note: 'Auditor recommendations for threshold adjustments, logic refinements, or parameter changes to improve rule effectiveness or reduce false positives. Explicitly identified in detection reasoning.']
  validation_methodology varchar [note: 'Audit testing approach used to validate this rule during the engagement (e.g., transaction sampling, back-testing, scenario analysis, model validation). Explicitly identified in detection reasoning.']
  validation_status varchar [note: 'Current status of the validation testing for this rule within this engagement lifecycle.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the validation testing relationship between monitoring_rule and engagement. It captures the audit testing and validation activities performed on AML/BSA monitoring rules during internal audit engagements. Each record links one monitoring rule to one audit engagement with validation results, effectiveness assessments, and tuning recommendations that exist only in the context of this specific audit test.. Existence Justification: In banking audit operations, a single AML/BSA audit engagement routinely validates multiple monitoring rules (e.g., an annual AML audit tests structuring detection, rapid movement, high-risk geography, and peer group anomaly rules). Conversely, a single monitoring rule is validated across multiple audit engagements over time (annual AML audits, model validation engagements, continuous monitoring reviews, regulatory response audits). The business actively manages rule validation testing as an operational process, tracking effectiveness ratings, false positive rates, alert volumes reviewed, and tuning recommendations for each rule-engagement combination.'
}

Table compliance.coverage {
  coverage_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique identifier for this audit coverage record. Primary key.']
  compliance_obligation_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the compliance obligation being tested in this audit engagement']
  engagement_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the internal audit engagement that tests this obligation']
  actual_test_hours decimal(8,2) [note: 'Actual audit hours expended testing this specific obligation within this engagement. Used for variance analysis and future planning.']
  audit_scope_description varchar [note: 'Detailed description of how this specific obligation is scoped and tested within this engagement, including specific controls tested, sample sizes, time periods covered, and any scope limitations.']
  coverage_status varchar [note: 'Current status of this coverage record: planned (scheduled but not started), in progress (testing underway), completed (testing finished), deferred (postponed to future engagement), or cancelled (removed from scope).']
  findings_count bigint [note: 'Number of audit findings or exceptions identified for this obligation during this engagement. Used for risk assessment and remediation tracking.']
  last_test_date date [note: 'The date when testing of this obligation was last completed within this engagement. Used to track testing currency and plan future coverage.']
  next_test_due_date date [note: 'The scheduled date when this obligation must be tested again, based on the testing frequency and risk rating. Used for audit planning and coverage gap analysis.']
  percentage decimal(5,2) [note: 'Percentage of the obligation scope covered by this specific engagement (0-100). Allows tracking partial coverage when a single engagement tests only certain aspects of an obligation.']
  planned_test_hours decimal(8,2) [note: 'Budgeted audit hours allocated to testing this specific obligation within this engagement. Used for resource planning and variance analysis.']
  test_frequency_months bigint [note: 'The required testing frequency for this obligation in months (e.g., 12 for annual, 36 for triennial). Drives audit planning and coverage scheduling.']
  test_result varchar [note: 'The outcome of testing this obligation within this engagement: compliant, non-compliant, partially compliant, not tested, or in progress.']
  testing_approach varchar [note: 'The audit methodology used to test this obligation within this engagement: substantive testing, control testing, walkthrough, inquiry and observation, data analytics, sampling, or full population review.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the testing relationship between a compliance obligation and an internal audit engagement. It captures the scope, timing, and approach used to test each obligation within each audit engagement. Each record links one obligation to one engagement with attributes that exist only in the context of this testing relationship, enabling the bank to track which obligations are covered by which audits, when they were tested, and what testing approach was used.. Existence Justification: In banking audit and compliance operations, a single internal audit engagement routinely tests multiple regulatory obligations (e.g., a BSA/AML engagement covers CTR filing, SAR filing, CIP, and CDD obligations simultaneously), and conversely, a single compliance obligation requires testing across multiple audit engagements throughout the year (e.g., SOX 404 control testing spans quarterly IT audits, annual financial audits, and specialized process audits). The business actively manages this coverage relationship through audit planning, tracks testing approach and timing for each obligation-engagement pair, and refers to this as the Audit Coverage Mapping or Obligation Testing Matrix.'
}

  remarks varchar [note: 'Additional remarks, notes, or contextual information provided by the sanctions authority regarding the entry.']
  risk_score decimal(5,2) [note: 'Numeric risk score assigned to the sanctions list entry based on severity, program type, and other risk factors. Scale typically 0-100.']
  screening_priority varchar [note: 'Priority level assigned for real-time transaction screening and customer due diligence checks based on risk and regulatory requirements.']

Table channel.sla {
  sla_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for sla']
  channel_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the customer interaction channel (digital banking, branch, ATM, contact center, relationship manager, API/open banking) to which this SLA applies.']
  channel_interaction_id varchar [note: 'Reference identifier of the specific customer interaction or transaction that experienced the SLA breach.']
  sla_breach_id varchar [note: 'Unique identifier for a specific SLA breach instance; null if this record is an SLA definition rather than a breach event.']
  actual_resolution_time_minutes varchar [note: 'Actual time in minutes taken to fully resolve customer interaction; used to compare against target for breach detection.']
  actual_response_time_minutes varchar [note: 'Actual time in minutes taken to provide initial response to customer interaction; used to compare against target for breach detection.']
  breach_penalty_amount decimal(15,2) [note: 'Monetary penalty or credit applied to customer or internal cost center as a result of the SLA breach.']
  breach_penalty_currency_code varchar [note: 'Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the breach penalty amount.']
  breach_severity varchar [note: 'Severity classification of the SLA breach based on magnitude of delay and customer impact.']
  breach_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when the SLA breach occurred.']
  breach_type varchar [note: 'Type of SLA breach that occurred (response time exceeded, resolution time exceeded, escalation threshold breached).']
  channel_type varchar [note: 'Type of customer interaction channel covered by this SLA.']
  created_by_user varchar [note: 'Username or identifier of the user who created this SLA record.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when this SLA record (definition or breach event) was first created in the system.']
  customer_impact_assessment varchar [note: 'Assessment of the impact of the SLA breach on customer experience, satisfaction, and business relationship.']
  effective_from_date date [note: 'Date from which this SLA definition becomes active and enforceable.']
  effective_to_date date [note: 'Date until which this SLA definition remains active; null indicates open-ended SLA.']
  escalation_threshold_minutes varchar [note: 'Time threshold in minutes after which unresolved interaction must be escalated to higher support tier or management.']
  interaction_category varchar [note: 'Category of customer interaction or transaction type covered by this SLA (e.g., account inquiry, loan application, wire transfer, complaint).']
  measurement_methodology varchar [note: 'Description of how SLA performance is measured and calculated (e.g., business hours vs. calendar hours, start/end event definitions).']
  regulator_case_number varchar [note: 'Case or reference number assigned by the regulatory authority if the breach was escalated or reported.']
  regulatory_basis varchar [note: 'Regulatory requirement or standard that mandates or informs this SLA (e.g., CFPB complaint resolution timelines, OCC service standards).']
  remediation_action_taken varchar [note: 'Description of corrective or remediation actions taken in response to the SLA breach.']
  reported_to_regulator_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this SLA breach was reported to a regulatory authority (CFPB, OCC) as part of compliance reporting.']
  responsible_channel varchar [note: 'Name or identifier of the channel or operational unit responsible for the breach.']
  responsible_team varchar [note: 'Name or identifier of the team or department responsible for the breach.']
  root_cause_category varchar [note: 'Categorized root cause of the SLA breach (system outage, staffing shortage, process failure, high volume, training gap, third-party delay).']
  root_cause_description varchar [note: 'Detailed narrative description of the root cause analysis findings for the SLA breach.']
  sla_name varchar [note: 'Business-friendly name of the SLA definition (e.g., \'Mobile Banking Account Inquiry Response Time\', \'Branch Complaint Resolution SLA\').']
  sla_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the SLA definition.']
  target_resolution_time_minutes varchar [note: 'Target time in minutes for complete resolution of customer interaction or request.']
  target_response_time_minutes varchar [note: 'Target time in minutes for initial response to customer interaction or request.']
  updated_by_user varchar [note: 'Username or identifier of the user who last updated this SLA record.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when this SLA record was last modified.']

  Note: 'Master record defining SLA targets and thresholds for each channel and interaction type combination, including breach event tracking. Captures SLA name, channel type, interaction category (account inquiry, loan application, wire transfer, complaint), target response time, target resolution time, escalation thresholds, measurement methodology, effective date range, and regulatory basis (CFPB complaint resolution timelines, OCC service standards). Also records each SLA breach instance: breach type (response time, resolution time, escalation), actual vs. target metric, breach severity, root cause category, responsible channel/team, remediation action taken, customer impact assessment, and breach penalty applied. Feeds SLA monitoring dashboards, regulatory reporting (CFPB complaint SLA compliance), and operational improvement programs.'
}

Table channel.sla_breach {
  sla_breach_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique identifier for the SLA breach record.']
  audit_finding_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to audit.finding. Business justification: SLA breaches are frequently cited as evidence in audit findings related to operational risk, customer service failures, and control deficiencies. Auditors link breaches to findings for root cause anal']
  channel_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the channel where the SLA breach occurred (mobile, web, branch, ATM, contact center).']
  interaction_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the customer interaction or case that triggered the SLA breach.']
  operational_risk_event_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to risk.operational_risk_event. Business justification: Material SLA breaches trigger operational risk event logging for regulatory reporting (operational loss data collection) and root cause analysis. Banks must track SLA failures as operational risk even']
  party_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the customer or party affected by the SLA breach.']
  primary_sla_responsible_employee_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the employee or relationship manager responsible for handling the interaction that breached the SLA.']
  related_compliance_compliance_breach_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to compliance.breach. Business justification: Channel SLA breaches that violate regulatory commitments (Reg E error resolution timing, complaint response deadlines, accessibility requirements) escalate to compliance breaches. Link enables regulat']
  actual_metric_value decimal(18,4) [note: 'The actual metric value achieved, which exceeded the SLA target (e.g., 45 seconds, 3 hours, 2 business days).']
  breach_reference_number varchar [note: 'Externally-known unique reference number for the SLA breach incident.']
  breach_severity varchar [note: 'Severity classification of the SLA breach based on impact and deviation magnitude.']
  breach_status varchar [note: 'Current status of the SLA breach in the remediation workflow.']
  breach_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The exact date and time when the SLA target was breached.']
  breach_type varchar [note: 'Type of SLA metric that was breached (response time, resolution time, escalation time, acknowledgment time, callback time, processing time).']
  business_line varchar [note: 'The line of business or business unit where the SLA breach occurred (retail banking, investment banking, wealth management, etc.).']
  channel_sla_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the SLA definition that was breached.']
  closed_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when the SLA breach case was formally closed.']
  comments varchar [note: 'Additional notes or comments regarding the SLA breach incident and its handling.']
  compensation_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'Monetary value of compensation or credit offered to the customer for the SLA breach.']
  compensation_currency_code varchar [note: 'ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the compensation amount.']
  compensation_offered_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether compensation or goodwill gesture was offered to the customer due to the SLA breach.']
  country_code varchar [note: 'ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code where the SLA breach occurred.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when this SLA breach record was first created in the system.']
  customer_impact_assessment varchar [note: 'Assessment of the impact of the SLA breach on the customer experience and satisfaction.']
  customer_notification_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when the customer was notified about the SLA breach.']
  customer_notified_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the customer was notified about the SLA breach.']
  detected_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when the SLA breach was detected by the monitoring system.']
  deviation_percentage decimal(5,2) [note: 'The percentage deviation from the SLA target ((actual - target) / target * 100).']
  deviation_value decimal(18,4) [note: 'The magnitude of deviation from the SLA target (actual minus target).']
  escalation_level varchar [note: 'The escalation tier or level reached during the breach handling process (0 = no escalation, 1 = first level, 2 = second level, etc.).']
  geographic_region varchar [note: 'The geographic region or market where the SLA breach occurred.']
  last_modified_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when this SLA breach record was last updated.']
  metric_unit varchar [note: 'Unit of measure for the SLA metric (seconds, minutes, hours, business days, calendar days).']
  product_category varchar [note: 'The product or service category associated with the interaction that breached the SLA (deposits, loans, payments, investments, etc.).']
  regulatory_report_submission_date date [note: 'The date when the regulatory report was submitted.']
  regulatory_report_submitted_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether a regulatory report has been submitted for this SLA breach.']
  regulatory_reportable_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this SLA breach is reportable to regulatory bodies such as Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) for complaint SLA compliance.']
  remediation_action_taken varchar [note: 'Description of the corrective or remediation action taken to address the SLA breach.']
  remediation_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when remediation action was completed.']
  responsible_team varchar [note: 'The team or department responsible for the channel or process where the breach occurred.']
  root_cause_category varchar [note: 'Primary category of the root cause that led to the SLA breach.']
  root_cause_description varchar [note: 'Detailed description of the root cause analysis findings for the SLA breach.']
  target_metric_value decimal(18,4) [note: 'The SLA target metric value that was expected to be met (e.g., 30 seconds, 2 hours, 1 business day).']

  Note: 'Transactional record capturing each instance where a channel SLA target was breached. Captures the associated SLA definition, interaction or case reference, breach type (response time, resolution time, escalation), actual vs. target metric, breach severity, root cause category, responsible channel/team, remediation action taken, and customer impact assessment. Feeds regulatory reporting (CFPB complaint SLA compliance) and operational improvement programs.'
}

Table channel.journey {

  journey_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the journey instance. Tracks whether the customer is actively progressing, has completed, or has dropped off. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: initiated|in_progress|completed|abandoned|suspended|cancelled|failed — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  journey_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the journey by business process type. Determines applicable regulatory requirements, SLA targets, and channel orchestration rules. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: account_opening|loan_application|kyc_refresh|onboarding|product_upgrade|complaint_resolution|service_request|wealth_advisory|investment_onboarding — 9 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']

  total_duration_minutes varchar [note: 'Total elapsed time from journey start to completion or abandonment, measured in minutes. Used for performance analysis and SLA compliance.']
  total_stages varchar [note: 'Total number of stages defined in the journey template. Used to calculate journey completion percentage.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when this journey record was last modified. Used for audit trail and change tracking.']

  Note: 'Master record defining standardized customer journey templates and tracking individual customer journey instances for key banking processes — account opening, loan application, onboarding, KYC refresh, product upgrade, and complaint resolution. Template layer captures journey name, channel scope (omnichannel, digital-only, branch-only), journey stages, expected duration per stage, handoff rules between channels, drop-off thresholds, and associated regulatory requirements (CFPB, OCC). Instance layer tracks each customer\'s progression: customer ID, journey template reference, current stage, channel at each stage, timestamps for stage entry/exit, stage outcomes, channel switches (e.g., started online, completed in branch), abandonment flags, NPS score collected, and final journey outcome. Enables omnichannel journey orchestration, completion rate tracking, NPS measurement, CLTV-linked engagement analysis, and process improvement.'
}

  abandonment_stage_code varchar [note: 'Code of the stage where the customer abandoned the journey. Null if the journey was not abandoned. Used to identify high-friction stages and optimize journey design.']
  active_duration_seconds varchar [note: 'Total time in seconds the customer was actively engaged in the journey (excluding idle time, wait time for approvals, or system processing time). Measures actual customer effort.']
  branch_code varchar [note: 'Code of the branch where the journey was initiated or primarily executed. Null for fully digital journeys. Supports branch-level journey performance analysis.']
  campaign_code varchar [note: 'Marketing campaign code associated with this journey instance. Links journey performance to specific marketing initiatives and enables campaign Return on Investment (ROI) analysis.']
  channel_switch_count varchar [note: 'Number of times the customer switched channels during this journey. Indicates omnichannel engagement complexity and potential friction points.']
  cltv_segment varchar [note: 'Customer Lifetime Value (CLTV) segment of the customer at the time of journey initiation. Used to link journey experience and completion rates to customer value and prioritize high-value customer journeys.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this journey instance record was first created in the system. Used for data lineage and audit trail purposes.']
  current_channel_code varchar [note: 'Channel where the customer is currently interacting in the journey. Tracks channel switches and omnichannel behavior (e.g., started online, continued in branch). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: mobile|web|branch|atm|contact_center|relationship_manager|api|partner — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  current_stage_code varchar [note: 'Code representing the current stage in the journey where the customer is positioned (e.g., \'INIT\', \'KYC\', \'APPROVAL\', \'FULFILLMENT\', \'COMPLETE\'). Used for operational tracking and stage-level analytics.']
  current_stage_entry_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when the customer entered the current stage. Used to track stage-level duration and identify bottlenecks in the journey progression.']
  current_stage_name varchar [note: 'Human-readable name of the current stage (e.g., \'Initial Application\', \'Know Your Customer (KYC) Verification\', \'Credit Approval\', \'Account Fulfillment\'). Provides business context for the current position in the journey.']
  customer_feedback_text varchar [note: 'Free-text feedback provided by the customer about their journey experience. Supports qualitative analysis of customer sentiment and journey pain points.']
  customer_segment_code varchar [note: 'Code representing the customer segment (e.g., \'RETAIL\', \'WEALTH\', \'CORPORATE\', \'SME\') at the time of journey initiation. Enables segment-specific journey performance analysis.']
  device_type varchar [note: 'Type of device used by the customer to initiate the journey. Supports device-specific journey optimization and responsive design analytics.']
  end_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when the journey was completed, abandoned, or terminated. Null for in-progress journeys. Used to calculate journey duration and completion metrics.']
  error_count varchar [note: 'Number of errors or exceptions encountered during the journey. Indicates technical friction and system reliability issues impacting customer experience.']
  final_outcome_code varchar [note: 'Final outcome of the journey instance. Indicates whether the customer successfully completed the intended business objective, failed, partially completed, or abandoned.']
  final_outcome_description varchar [note: 'Detailed description of the final journey outcome. Provides business context for the outcome code (e.g., \'Account opened successfully\', \'Application declined due to credit score\', \'Customer abandoned at document upload\').']
  journey_name varchar [note: 'Business-friendly name of the journey being tracked (e.g., \'Personal Loan Application\', \'Wealth Management Onboarding\', \'Credit Card Activation\'). Provides human-readable context for reporting and analytics.']
  journey_status varchar [note: 'Overall lifecycle status of the journey instance. Indicates whether the customer is actively progressing, has completed, abandoned, or encountered issues in the journey.']
  last_modified_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this journey instance record was last updated. Tracks the most recent change to the journey state for audit and data quality purposes.']
  nps_collection_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when the NPS score was collected from the customer. Null if NPS was not collected for this journey instance.']
  nps_score varchar [note: 'Net Promoter Score (NPS) collected from the customer at journey completion. Scale of 0-10 measuring customer satisfaction and likelihood to recommend. Used to link journey experience to customer loyalty metrics.']
  product_code varchar [note: 'Code of the banking product or service associated with this journey (e.g., \'CHECKING_ACCT\', \'PERSONAL_LOAN\', \'WEALTH_ADVISORY\'). Links journey instances to product performance and cross-sell analytics.']
  product_name varchar [note: 'Human-readable name of the banking product or service associated with this journey. Provides business context for product-specific journey analytics.']
  referral_source_code varchar [note: 'Code indicating how the customer was referred to this journey (e.g., \'ORGANIC\', \'CAMPAIGN\', \'PARTNER\', \'BRANCH_REFERRAL\'). Supports marketing attribution and channel effectiveness analysis.']
  retry_count varchar [note: 'Number of times the customer retried a stage or action during the journey. Indicates usability issues or customer confusion at specific journey stages.']
  sla_met_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the journey was completed within the SLA target duration. True if total_duration_seconds is less than or equal to sla_target_duration_seconds.']
  sla_target_duration_seconds varchar [note: 'Target duration in seconds for completing this journey as defined by the Service Level Agreement (SLA). Used to measure journey performance against business commitments.']
  stage_count varchar [note: 'Total number of stages the customer progressed through in this journey instance. Used to measure journey complexity and compare actual vs. expected stage progression.']
  start_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when the customer initiated this journey instance. Marks the beginning of the customer\'s progression through the defined journey template.']
  total_duration_seconds varchar [note: 'Total elapsed time in seconds from journey start to end. Calculated as the difference between end_timestamp and start_timestamp. Used for journey efficiency analysis and Service Level Agreement (SLA) tracking.']

  Note: 'Transactional record tracking each individual customer\'s progression through a defined journey template. Captures customer ID, journey template reference, current stage, channel at each stage, timestamps for stage entry/exit, stage outcomes, channel switches (e.g., started online, completed in branch), abandonment flags, NPS score collected, and final journey outcome. Enables omnichannel journey completion tracking and CLTV-linked engagement measurement.'
}

  terminal_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the ATM terminal type: branch (inside bank branch), offsite (standalone location), mobile (portable ATM), kiosk (self-service banking kiosk), or drive-through.']
  transaction_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'Principal monetary amount of the ATM transaction in the transaction currency, excluding any surcharges or fees.']
  transaction_currency_code varchar [note: 'Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the transaction amount (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP).']

  transaction_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when the ATM transaction was initiated by the customer at the terminal, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX).']
  transaction_type varchar [note: 'Type of ATM transaction performed: cash withdrawal, deposit, balance inquiry, PIN change, mini statement, cardless cash, inter-bank transfer, or bill payment. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: withdrawal|deposit|balance_inquiry|pin_change|mini_statement|cardless_cash|inter_bank_transfer|bill_payment — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this transaction record was last modified in the data platform, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX).']

  Note: 'Transactional record of each ATM transaction event — cash withdrawal, deposit, balance inquiry, PIN change, cardless cash, and inter-bank transfers. Captures ATM ID, card number (tokenized), customer reference, transaction type, amount, currency, network used (Visa/Mastercard/STAR), authorization code, response code, surcharge applied, cash dispensed flag, timestamp, and transaction status. Distinct from payment domain wire/ACH — this is ATM-channel-specific card-present transaction capture.'
}

  customer_device_fingerprint varchar [note: 'Unique identifier of the device used by the customer to grant consent, supporting fraud detection and security monitoring.']

  data_access_log_reference varchar [note: 'Reference identifier linking to detailed audit logs of all data access events performed under this consent, enabling full traceability.']
  data_retention_period_days varchar [note: 'Number of days the consent record and associated audit logs must be retained for regulatory compliance after consent expiry or revocation.']
  effective_from_date date [note: 'Date from which the consent becomes active and the TPP is authorized to access customer data.']
  expiry_date date [note: 'Date on which the consent automatically expires and data access authorization terminates, typically 90 days from grant under PSD2.']
  grant_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when the customer granted the open banking consent, recorded in ISO 8601 format with timezone.']
  last_access_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time of the most recent data access by the TPP under this consent, used for monitoring and compliance reporting.']
  last_modified_timestamp timestamp [note: 'System timestamp when this consent record was last updated, supporting audit trail and data lineage requirements.']
  notification_preference varchar [note: 'Customer preference for receiving notifications about consent status changes, access events, and expiry warnings: email, SMS, mobile push notification, or none.']
  recurring_access_indicator boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the consent authorizes recurring data access (true) or one-time access only (false).']
  regulatory_framework varchar [note: 'Regulatory framework under which the consent was granted: PSD2 (EU), CFPB Section 1033 (US), CDR (Australia), Open Banking UK, or other jurisdiction-specific framework.']
  renewal_indicator boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this consent is a renewal of a previous expired consent (true) or a new initial consent (false).']
  revocation_reason varchar [note: 'Reason provided by the customer or bank for revoking the consent, supporting audit and customer service requirements.']
  revocation_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when the customer revoked the consent, terminating TPP data access authorization. Null if consent has not been revoked.']
  risk_assessment_score decimal(5,2) [note: 'Risk score assigned to this consent at grant time based on customer profile, TPP reputation, and fraud indicators, ranging from 0.00 (low risk) to 100.00 (high risk).']
  source_system_code varchar [note: 'Identifier of the source system or API gateway that originated this consent record, enabling data lineage tracking across the enterprise.']
  tpp_certificate_reference varchar [note: 'Qualified certificate identifier issued to the TPP by a qualified trust service provider, validating TPP authorization under PSD2.']
  transaction_history_period_days varchar [note: 'Number of days of historical transaction data the TPP is authorized to access, typically 90 days under PSD2.']

  Note: 'Master record managing customer consent grants for open banking and API-based third-party data sharing under PSD2, CFPB Section 1033, and open banking frameworks. Captures customer ID, third-party provider (TPP) identity, consent scope (account data, payment initiation, identity), consent grant timestamp, expiry date, revocation status, data access log reference, regulatory framework (PSD2/CFPB 1033/CDR), and consent version. SSOT for open banking authorization and data sharing governance.'
}

Existence Justification: In banking internal audit operations, audit engagements routinely cover multiple branch locations (regional audits, thematic compliance reviews, network-wide cash audits), and each branch is subject to multiple audit engagements over time (annual operational audits, surprise cash counts, BSA/AML reviews, SOX testing). The audit function actively manages the scope definition by assigning branches to engagements, tracking branch-specific risk ratings, sample sizes, findings counts, and audit status per branch.'

Table channel.rule_configuration {
  rule_configuration_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique identifier for this channel-rule configuration record. Primary key.']
  banking_channel_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the banking channel where this rule configuration applies']
  detection_rule_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the fraud detection rule being configured for this channel']
  alert_volume varchar [note: 'Total number of fraud alerts generated by this rule on this channel during the measurement period, used for capacity planning and rule tuning decisions']
  channel_specific_threshold decimal(18,4) [note: 'Threshold value tuned specifically for this channel-rule combination, overriding the default rule threshold when channel risk profiles differ (e.g., ATM may have lower velocity thresholds than mobile banking)']
  configuration_status varchar [note: 'Operational status of this rule on this channel: active (in production), inactive (disabled for this channel), testing (pilot mode), suspended (temporarily disabled due to performance issues)']
  effective_date date [note: 'Date when this channel-specific rule configuration became active in production monitoring']
  expiration_date date [note: 'Date when this channel-specific configuration is scheduled for review or retirement. Null for ongoing configurations.']
  false_positive_rate decimal(5,4) [note: 'Proportion of legitimate transactions on this channel incorrectly flagged by this rule, calculated as false positives divided by total alerts for this channel-rule pair']
  last_tuning_date date [note: 'Date when the channel-specific threshold or configuration was last adjusted based on performance analysis for this channel-rule combination']
  measurement_period_end_date date [note: 'End date of the performance measurement period for the channel-specific metrics']
  measurement_period_start_date date [note: 'Start date of the performance measurement period for the channel-specific metrics (alert_volume, false_positive_rate, effectiveness_score)']
  rule_effectiveness_score decimal(5,2) [note: 'Composite effectiveness metric (0-100) for this rule on this specific channel, calculated from channel-specific true positive rate, false positive rate, and detection coverage']

  Note: 'This association product represents the configuration relationship between banking channels and fraud detection rules. It captures channel-specific rule tuning, performance metrics, and threshold adjustments that exist only in the context of a specific channel-rule pairing. Each record links one channel to one detection rule with performance data and configuration parameters that vary by channel.. Existence Justification: In banking fraud operations, detection rules are configured and tuned differently for each channel based on channel-specific fraud patterns and risk profiles. A single fraud detection rule (e.g., velocity check) applies to multiple channels (ATM, mobile, branch, wire), and each channel has multiple active rules. The bank actively manages channel-rule configurations as operational entities, tracking performance metrics (alert volume, false positive rate, effectiveness score) and tuning thresholds per channel-rule combination.'
}

Table channel.cost_allocation {
  cost_allocation_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique identifier for this cost center to channel allocation relationship. Primary key.']
  approved_by_employee_id varchar [note: 'Identifier of the finance manager or controller who approved this cost allocation relationship. Used for audit trail and governance of allocation methodology changes.']
  banking_channel_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the banking channel receiving cost allocations']
  cost_center_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the cost center that is allocating costs to the channel']
  created_by_user_employee_id varchar [note: 'User ID of the person who created this cost allocation record. Used for audit trail and accountability.']
  last_modified_by_user_employee_id varchar [note: 'User ID of the person who last modified this cost allocation record. Used for audit trail and accountability.']
  allocation_amount_annual decimal(18,2) [note: 'Budgeted or actual annual cost amount allocated from this cost center to this channel in the reporting currency. Calculated as cost_center.budget_amount * allocation_percentage. Used for channel P&L reporting and profitability analysis.']
  allocation_method varchar [note: 'Method used to calculate the allocation of costs from this cost center to this channel. Direct allocation assigns costs based on direct usage or causation. Activity-based uses cost drivers. Headcount allocates based on FTE count. Transaction volume uses transaction counts. Revenue-based allocates proportional to channel revenue. Square footage uses physical space. Custom indicates a specialized allocation formula.']
  allocation_percentage decimal(5,2) [note: 'Percentage of the cost center\'s total costs allocated to this specific channel. Used for proportional cost distribution in activity-based costing. Sum of allocation_percentage across all channels for a given cost_center should equal 100%.']
  allocation_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of this cost allocation relationship. Active allocations are used in current financial reporting. Pending allocations are approved but not yet effective. Suspended allocations are temporarily inactive. Closed allocations are historical and no longer used.']
  approval_date date [note: 'Date when this cost allocation relationship was formally approved by finance management. Used for audit trail and compliance with internal financial controls.']
  cost_driver_metric varchar [note: 'The specific business metric or cost driver used to determine the allocation percentage for activity-based costing methods (e.g., transaction_count, customer_count, FTE_count, square_feet, server_hours). Null for direct allocation methods.']
  cost_driver_value decimal(18,4) [note: 'The quantitative value of the cost driver metric for this cost center-channel allocation (e.g., 15000 transactions, 250 FTEs, 5000 square feet). Used to calculate allocation_percentage when using activity-based methods.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this cost allocation record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail.']
  effective_from_date date [note: 'Date when this cost allocation relationship became active and began being used for financial reporting and profitability analysis. Supports temporal tracking of allocation changes over time.']
  effective_to_date date [note: 'Date when this cost allocation relationship ended or was superseded by a new allocation structure. Null for currently active allocations. Supports historical analysis of cost allocation changes.']
  last_modified_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this cost allocation record was last updated. Used for audit trail and change tracking.']
  notes varchar [note: 'Free-text notes explaining the business rationale for this specific allocation, any special considerations, or documentation of allocation methodology decisions. Used for knowledge transfer and audit support.']
  primary_channel_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this channel is the primary recipient of costs from this cost center. Used when a cost center predominantly supports one channel but has minor allocations to others. Supports simplified reporting and primary cost center assignment for channels.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the cost allocation relationship between cost centers and banking channels. It captures how organizational costs are distributed across customer interaction channels for activity-based costing, channel profitability analysis, and management accounting. Each record links one cost center to one channel with allocation percentages, methods, and effective date ranges that exist only in the context of this cost distribution relationship.. Existence Justification: In banking operations, cost centers (organizational units like IT Operations, Compliance, Facilities) distribute their costs across multiple channels (branch network, ATM network, digital channels, contact centers), and each channel receives cost allocations from multiple cost centers. Banks actively manage these allocation relationships through formal allocation methodologies (activity-based costing, headcount-based, transaction volume-based) with specific percentages, effective dates, and approval workflows. This is a core management accounting process for channel profitability analysis, RAROC reporting, and FTP allocation.'
}
